body.en: *Business ethics* refers to the socially determined moral principles that should govern business activities: honesty, fairness, respect for others and for the law. Ethical behaviour builds trust among customers, employees, investors and the public, and so supports long-term success. Unethical practices include adulteration, hoarding, black-marketing, misleading advertisements, tax evasion, under-weighing and exploiting workers.

body.en: Ethical conduct protects consumers' interests, increases public confidence, improves the work culture (employees take pride in an honest employer), strengthens relations with suppliers and investors, and reduces the risk of legal penalties and scandals. In the long run, *ethics* and profit go together: a reputation takes years to build and minutes to lose.

problem.en: A shopkeeper sells packets marked 1 kg that weigh 950 g. Explain why this is unethical and what it may lead to.

steps.en: It deceives consumers, who pay for goods they do not receive.
It breaks the law on weights and measures and consumer protection.
If discovered, it can bring penalties, complaints and loss of customers.
It damages the trust on which the business depends.

answer.en: Under-weighing is cheating; it invites legal action and destroys the shop's reputation.
